alignments.note: Explicit subject pronoun takes only its own English; the copula joins the predicate (rule 20).

The verbless clause's supplied copula joins the predicate, which is the construct בֶּן heading the age phrase (rule 20); the construct itself is what the ASV renders by old. Discontinuous around the numeral and counted noun (rule 25), headed on the word realizing its lexeme rather than on the auxiliary (rule 24).
The ASV writes a demonstrative where the phrase's the would stand, and no other morpheme licenses it, so the article takes this and heads on it (rule 41).
Adverbial accusative noun day (rule 33).
Numeral eighty rendered fourscore.
Counted noun years.
The fronted question auxiliary can belongs to the interrogative particle, not to the verb (rule 17).
Verb with its subject pronoun (rule 17), headed on the lexical verb; the modal went to הֲ above.
בֵּין as between; rule 26 reads the connective the ASV actually writes.
Substantival adjective good.
The לְ of the בֵּין ... לְ frame takes the connective the ASV writes for it, and (rules 11, 26).
Substantival adjective rendered bad.
The אִם opening a following disjunctive question takes the fronted auxiliary can, exactly as rule 17's will ye not tremble gives will to אִם; the ASV writes no or here.
Suffix as possessive (rule 18).
Host noun servant.
Verb taste; its modal went to the interrogative אִם.
Object marker with no English of its own (rule 16).
The present relative takes the headless-relative pronoun what, before a supplied reading would (rule 46's first rider).
Verb with its subject pronoun (rule 17).
Waw rendered by the connective or (rule 14).
Object marker with no English of its own (rule 16).
Relative as what (rule 46).
Verb with its subject pronoun (rule 17).
The אִם of the next disjunctive question takes the fronted can (rule 17), as with the first.
Verb with its subject pronoun (rule 17).
עוֹד rendered by the two-word any more, headed on the lexeme-bearing word (rules 24, 31).
The ASV promotes the object of בְּ to a bare direct object, hear the voice, leaving the preposition no English word (rule 40).
Construct noun voice; no article morpheme stands in the chain, so the supplied the belongs to the nominal expression (rules 15, 29).
Nomen rectum takes the of-expression (rule 19); the participle is rendered by singing men, whose lexeme is carried by singing, since men alone is any men (rule 31).
Conjunctive waw (rule 14).
Feminine participle rendered singing women, headed on the lexeme-bearing word (rule 31).
לָמָּה rendered by the one English word wherefore: rule 30 fusion, headed on the interrogative carrying the lexeme. Recorded noncompositional, with the chapter's five other לָמָה units.

Waw rendered by the connective then, which the ASV writes after the interrogative; distance is not evidence against it (rules 14, 51). The competing reading marks the waw unrepresented and then added, but rule 14 reads the connective off the ASV where a waw is present to license it.
Verb with its supplied modal (rule 17); discontinuous around the explicit subject noun (rule 25), headed on the lexical verb.
Suffix as possessive (rule 18).
Host noun servant, the clause's explicit subject.
עוֹד as yet.
Resultative הָיָה לְ recast with a plain be, which belongs to הָיָה; the recasting leaves the preposition no English word (rules 21, 40).
Noun burden; Hebrew has no indefinite article, so a belongs to the noun that licenses it (rule 15).
Preposition unto (rule 11).
Suffix as possessive (rule 18).
Host noun lord.
Article takes the written the (rule 15).
Noun king.

review_notes: Only the status of the לָמָּה unit changed; its edges and heads are as the verse pass returned them, and no other unit was touched.
Every source and target ID is partitioned exactly once; four unrepresented units (s017, s021, s027, s039) and no added units.

Both occurrences of אִם open disjunctive questions and take the fronted can under rule 17; the interrogative הֲ takes the first can on the same terms, so all three English modals answer to interrogative morphemes rather than to the verbs.

The age formula בֶּן שְׁמֹנִים שָׁנָה is split three ways with the supplied copula on בֶּן as the predicate's anchor (rule 20); the alternative of treating old as construction-supplied and בֶּן unrepresented was rejected because old is what the construct itself is rendered by.
